description.narrative:
World Cities Day was established on 27 December 2013 by a United Nations General Assembly resolution in which the General Assembly "decides to designate 31 October, beginning in 2014, as World Cities Day, invites States, the United Nations system, in particular UN-Habitat, relevant international organizations, civil society and all relevant stakeholders to observe and raise awareness of the Day". The first World Cities Day was held in October 2014 and ties in with Sustainable Development Goal 11, to make cities "inclusive, safe, resilient and sustainable". The general theme of World Cities Day is Better City, Better Life, while this year the sub-theme is Adapting cities for climate resilience. Countries and cities around the world are encouraged to celebrate
This year UN-Habitat is holding the Global Observance in Luxor with the co-host of the Government of Egypt. There will be a high-level morning ceremony and four-afternoon roundtables. The main accomplishment is to raise global, regional, and national awareness around the urgent need to improve the climate resilience and adaptation of cities and exchange solutions • Accomplishments are providing support to national and local authorities to • Take urgent action to combat climate change and its impacts • Integrate climate change adaptation and resilience measures into national policies, strategies, and planning • Improve education, awareness-raising, and human and institutional capacity on climate change adaptation, impact reduction, and early warning • Gender markers • GEM1 - Contributes to gender equality/women’s
